functions.name: batch-delete-data-points
functions.description: Submit deletion of up to 100 identifiable health data points, including across data types, and return an honest aggregate processing receipt.

dataTypeId.description: Data type collection of this target; its category write grant is required.

dataPointId.description: Opaque target point ID within this data type.

items.description: An identifiable health data point belonging to the connected user.

targets.description: Distinct identifiable points to delete, all for the connected user. Public maximum 100, below the provider's documented 10000-target maximum.

FunctionInput_google_health_batchdeleted.description: One bounded batch of distinct identifiable health data points to delete.

status.description: Aggregate provider processing state; not an invented per-item outcome.

operationId.description: Opaque processing operation resource name when returned.

submittedCount.description: Number of distinct requested targets submitted, not number proven deleted.

FunctionOutput_google_health_batchdelete.description: Aggregate deletion processing receipt, without per-item outcomes or a deletion count.

tags.instructions: Use for up to 100 points belonging to the connected user. Obtain each dataTypeId and id from `list-data-points` or `get-data-point`. Use `delete-data-point` for one point. Deletion removes the records; no restore is exposed. The result is aggregate, not per-item success, and pending means processing is incomplete. All categories represented must be authorized.

functions.name: create-data-point
functions.description: Submit a new identifiable health data point and return whether its creation has completed or is still processing.

date.description: Primary calendar date for an applicable daily type; never converted to UTC.

endAt.description: Primary interval physical end, if applicable, with explicit offset and later than startAt.

values.description: Type-specific writable metric and descriptive fields, e.g. sleep type/stages/metadata or exercise exerciseType/displayName/metricsSummary. Supply domain objects directly; primary physical times/date belong above. Civil times and offset metadata can remain in their sampleTime/interval objects. Output-only fields cannot be supplied.

startAt.description: Primary interval physical start, if applicable, with explicit offset.

dataSource.description: Optional writable source metadata such as device and recordingMethod; output-only application/platform cannot be set.

dataTypeId.description: Identifiable data type to create; corresponding category write permission is required.

observedAt.description: Primary sample observation instant, if applicable, with explicit offset and at most nine fractional digits.

dataPointId.description: Optional client-chosen point ID, scoped to this user and data type; omission requests a system-generated ID.

FunctionInput_google_health_createdatapo.description: An identifiable health data point with structured writable values and its primary observation context.

status.description: pending means accepted for processing; completed means the provider reports successful completion, not merely submission.

dataTypeId.description: Data type targeted by the submission.

dataPointId.description: Known requested or returned point ID; may be absent for a pending system-assigned creation.

operationId.description: Opaque provider operation resource name when supplied; retain for support or later operation-status access, not a data-point ID.

FunctionOutput_google_health_createdatap.description: A single creation submission receipt, distinguishing acceptance from successful completion.

tags.instructions: Use only for identifiable data types supported for creation. Supply ordinary structured metric values, not a DataPoint envelope. Use `update-data-point` for an existing point. Keep a chosen dataPointId to check uncertain outcomes with `get-data-point`; do not blindly repeat a pending or ambiguous creation. A pending receipt establishes acceptance, not completed creation.

status.description: pending means deletion was accepted; completed means the provider reports successful completion.

operationId.description: Opaque processing operation resource name when returned.

FunctionOutput_google_health_deletedatap.description: Processing receipt for the submitted single-point deletion.

tags.instructions: Get dataTypeId and id from `list-data-points` or `get-data-point`. This removes the health record, not just an association; no undo is exposed. Use `batch-delete-data-points` for multiple targets. Only points this application is permitted to delete can be removed. A pending receipt means deletion has not yet been confirmed complete.

functions.name: delete-subscriber
functions.description: Request deletion of a notification endpoint registration, optionally including its user subscriptions. Reports whether the provider has completed deletion or is still processing it.

id.description: Full resource identifier of the subscriber targeted by the accepted deletion request.

Set deleteSubscriptions only when child user subscriptions should also be removed; otherwise existing children block deletion. Use `delete-subscription` to remove only one user association. A pending result is not completed deletion: inspect `list-subscribers` later rather than assuming notifications have stopped. No restore operation is available.

functions.name: delete-subscription
functions.description: Delete an existing user notification subscription, stopping notifications for that user to its subscriber. This removes the registration, not the user's health records.

FunctionInput_google_health_deletesubscr.description: The existing user notification subscription to delete.

id.description: Full resource ID of the subscription whose deletion the provider acknowledged.

FunctionOutput_google_health_deletesubsc.description: Acknowledgment of notification subscription deletion, not deletion of health records.

tags.instructions: Use this to stop notifications for one existing user subscription. Obtain its full subscription ID from `list-subscriptions`. Use `delete-subscriber` instead to remove an entire endpoint registration. No restore operation is available here; deletion does not remove underlying health data.

functions.name: download-shl-resource

dataSourceFamily.description: Source family to reconcile; omission preserves the provider's scope-dependent default.

FunctionInput_google_health_listreconcil.description: Select a data type, optional time boundaries and source family, and one reconciled page.

id.description: Underlying recorded point ID when the provider supplies dataPointName; absent otherwise.

date.description: Daily measurement's calendar date, when present.

endAt.description: Interval physical end in UTC Z, when present.

values.description: Type-specific reconciled metrics and descriptions; preserves nested fields, civil times and offsets after lifting primary physical times/date. Exact int64 values remain decimal strings.

startAt.description: Interval physical start in UTC Z, when present.

dataTypeId.description: Data type of this reconciled measurement.

observedAt.description: Sample physical observation instant in UTC Z, when present.

items.description: A reconciled measurement with primary physical times lifted from its type-specific metrics.
One provider page of reconciled measurements, in provider order.

nextCursor.description: Opaque continuation; absent when provider token is absent or empty.

FunctionOutput_google_health_listreconci.description: One reconciled health stream page and an optional continuation for the unchanged query.

tags.instructions: Use this to avoid combining overlapping sources yourself. Use `list-data-points` for raw recorded points and source metadata. Pass nextCursor back as cursor with unchanged arguments. Exercise and sleep allow at most 25 points per page. Reconciliation is a read and does not rewrite stored points.

functions.name: list-subscribers
functions.description: Inspect one page of notification subscribers registered in a Google Cloud project, including endpoint, state, and data-type configuration.

limit.description: Maximum subscribers in this page; defaults to 50. The provider may return fewer.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation from this tool for the same project and limit; omit for the first page.

projectId.description: Owning Google Cloud project ID or project number, without the projects/ prefix; treated as an opaque string.

FunctionInput_google_health_listsubscrib.description: Project and optional page controls for inspecting notification subscribers.

id.description: Full resource identifier projects/{project}/subscribers/{subscriber}; retain intact for related tools.

state.description: Provider lifecycle state: STATE_UNSPECIFIED, UNVERIFIED, ACTIVE, or INACTIVE; future values are preserved.

configs.description: Data-type configurations; omitted if absent, with an explicit empty list preserved.

items.description: Configured data-type name.

dataTypes.description: Configured data-type names in provider kebab-case.

subscriptionCreatePolicy.description: Provider creation policy, including AUTOMATIC, MANUAL, or SUBSCRIPTION_CREATE_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED; unknown values are preserved.

items.description: Data-type configuration and subscription creation policy.

createdAt.description: Creation instant normalized to UTC Z, preserving available fractional-second precision; omitted if absent.

updatedAt.description: Last modification instant normalized to UTC Z, preserving available fractional-second precision; omitted if absent.

authorizationSecretSet.description: Whether endpoint authorization has a secret configured; omitted if not reported. The secret itself is never returned.

items.description: Notification subscriber with safe endpoint authorization status.
Subscribers in this provider page; empty when none are returned.

totalSize.description: Provider-reported total number of subscribers matching the request; omitted if not supplied.

nextCursor.description: Opaque continuation for another page; omitted when exhausted.

FunctionOutput_google_health_listsubscri.description: One page of notification subscribers and any continuation.

tags.instructions: Use this to inspect existing notification endpoints and obtain subscriber IDs for `list-subscriptions` or `delete-subscriber`. You need the owning Google Cloud project ID or number. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` with the same project and limit to continue. Each call returns one page, not the whole project. Secrets are never returned.

functions.name: list-subscriptions
functions.description: Inspect one page of active user notification subscriptions for a subscriber, optionally selecting users and data types.

limit.description: Maximum subscriptions in this page, default 50; fewer may be returned.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation for the same subscriber, filters, and limit; omit for the first page.

userIds.description: Public health user IDs without users/; match any selected user. Omit for all users.

items.description: Public health user ID without the users/ prefix.

dataTypes.description: Provider data-type names, such as sleep or weight; match any selected type. Combined with userIds using AND. Omit for all types.

items.description: Provider data-type name.

subscriberId.description: Full subscriber resource ID from list-subscribers, including its owning project.

FunctionInput_google_health_listsubscrip.description: Select a subscriber and optional users, data types, and continuation for one page of active subscriptions.

userId.description: Public health user ID extracted from the users/{user} resource name; not an email address.

items.description: Data-type name extracted from a subscribed user data-type resource.

dataTypes.description: Subscribed data-type names, extracted from users/{health_user_id}/dataTypes/{data_type}; [] when no types are reported.

subscriberId.description: Full resource identifier of the owning subscriber.

items.description: An active user notification subscription.
Existing subscriptions in this provider page; empty when none match.

nextCursor.description: Opaque continuation for another page; omitted when exhausted.

FunctionOutput_google_health_listsubscri.description: One provider page of active subscriptions and an optional scope-bound continuation.

tags.instructions: Use this to inspect existing user notification subscriptions, not to create notification delivery. Obtain the subscriber ID from `list-subscribers`. Optional user IDs are public health user IDs, not account email addresses. Pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` with all other arguments unchanged to continue. Use `delete-subscription` to stop one user's subscription.

functions.name: update-data-point
functions.description: Submit partial changes to an existing identifiable health data point and return its processing receipt.

dataTypeId.description: Identifiable data type containing the point.

dataPointId.description: Opaque existing point ID, scoped to the connected user and selected data type.

date.description: Replacement daily observation calendar date, when applicable.

endAt.description: Replacement primary interval end instant, with explicit offset.

values.description: Writable metric and descriptive fields to merge into the existing type-specific values; null clears an optional field and cannot clear required metrics.

startAt.description: Replacement primary interval start instant, with explicit offset.

dataSource.description: Writable source fields to merge; output-only provider attribution cannot be altered.

observedAt.description: Replacement primary sample physical observation instant, with explicit offset.

changes.description: Partial changes in the normalized read model. Omitted fields are preserved; null clears an optional writable field, empty arrays replace with empty, and objects merge recursively.

FunctionInput_google_health_updatedatapo.description: An existing identifiable health data point and the normalized fields to change.

status.description: pending means accepted for processing; completed means the provider reports successful processing.

dataPointId.description: Opaque identifier of the existing target.

operationId.description: Opaque provider operation resource name when returned; not a point ID.

FunctionOutput_google_health_updatedatap.description: The processing receipt for the submitted update; pending is not a completion guarantee.

tags.instructions: Get the data type and point ID from `list-data-points` or `get-data-point`. Only change data this application is permitted to edit. Omitted fields stay unchanged; supplied arrays replace their whole value. Use null only to clear an optional writable field. This can overwrite health information. A pending receipt means processing is not complete; inspect the point with `get-data-point` rather than blindly replaying an uncertain write.

functions.name: update-profile
functions.description: Partially update the connected user's manually configured running and walking stride lengths. Age, membership date and automatic stride calculations cannot be changed.

userConfiguredRunningStrideLengthMm.description: New manually configured running stride length in millimeters; omitted preserves it, null requests clearing the configured override where supported.

userConfiguredWalkingStrideLengthMm.description: New manually configured walking stride length in millimeters; omitted preserves it, null requests clearing where supported.

FunctionInput_google_health_updateprofil.description: Manual stride-length changes for the connected user; supply at least one field.

items.description: Public name of a manually configured stride field included in the successful update.

updatedFields.description: Public field names included in the successful update; this is not a claim that automatic stride mode changed.

userConfiguredRunningStrideLengthMm.description: Resulting configured running stride in millimeters when returned; omitted if cleared or not returned.

userConfiguredWalkingStrideLengthMm.description: Resulting configured walking stride in millimeters when returned; omitted if cleared or not returned.

FunctionOutput_google_health_updateprofi.description: Successfully updated manual stride fields and configured values returned by Google Health.

tags.instructions: Use for explicit manual stride values in millimeters. Use `get-profile` to inspect current values and `get-settings` to inspect automatic/manual stride mode, which this tool cannot change. Omitted values remain unchanged. Null resets a configured value only if the provider supports clearing; otherwise the tool reports unsupported_clear. This overwrites existing profile values.

functions.name: update-settings
functions.description: Partially update the connected user's writable measurement-unit preferences without changing other account settings.

swimUnit.description: Replacement swim-unit preference; omit to preserve, unspecified sets the provider's explicit unspecified enum.

waterUnit.description: Replacement water-unit preference; regional cup/fluid-ounce definitions are not changed or inferred.

temperatureUnit.description: Replacement temperature-unit preference. Null and empty strings are not clearing values.

FunctionInput_google_health_updatesettin.description: At least one writable measurement-unit preference to replace; omitted preferences remain unchanged.

swimUnit.description: Resulting swim preference when returned by the provider.

items.description: Public name of a measurement-unit preference included in the successful update mask.

updatedFields.description: Public names included in the successful update mask.

FunctionOutput_google_health_updatesetti.description: Preferences supplied by the successful write response and the public fields included in its update mask.

tags.instructions: Use for unit preferences only. Use `get-settings` to inspect current preferences; timezone, locale, food-language and stride mode cannot be changed here. Omitted fields remain unchanged. Explicit unspecified resets a unit to the provider's unspecified enum, not to a promised regional default. Existing preferences are overwritten.
